findings_verified.claim: the ?customerId= parameter on the customer self-service family is NOT a cross-tenant read - provider, foreign-customer and anonymous callers are all refused
findings_verified.what_the_hunt_did_not_cover: The original probe reached EIGHT routes and lived under /tmp, so it was neither reproducible nor representative: a sweep of app/api finds 54 routes that read a caller-supplied customerId. R01-e now asserts structurally that every one of them applies SOME authorization, and R01-f that the eight customer-facing ones specifically gate on ownership rather than on a bare permission - the W2-17 defect class, where bookings.view admitted any onboarded provider because the service_provider role holds it too.
findings_verified.measured: Of 54 routes reading a caller-supplied customerId, 31 use requireCustomerOwnership and 23 use a permission instead. Routes applying NEITHER: 0. The 23 are staff surfaces, where a permission is the correct gate.
findings_verified.cases: 24 behavioural cases (8 routes x provider session / foreign customer session / anonymous), all refused 401 or 403; R01-d non-vacuity proves the victim's OWN session passes the same gate and is refused for another id; R01-e and R01-f are the structural sweep.
findings_verified.sessions: Real platform sessions issued through the real issuePlatformSession and upsertIdentityBinding - partner_otp for the provider, customer_otp for both customers. No hand-forged cookie.

findings_verified.claim: the public contact-form abuse gate is not off-by-one or bypassable by a missing IP header - it admits exactly 5 per window and fails closed without an IP
cases: R03-01 the boundary is exactly 5 accepted then 429 - pinned, not merely 'some are refused'
R03-02 an absent cf-connecting-ip is refused rather than sharing one bucket
R03-03 an exhausted IP does not poison a different IP
R03-04 refused attempts keep counting, so the limit cannot be ridden back down
R03-05 the gate runs BEFORE the body parse, so unparseable bodies cannot flood past it
R03-06 NON-VACUITY: an honest first submission is accepted and writes a lead
findings_verified.note: `attempts > RATE_LIMIT` with RATE_LIMIT=5 is only correct because the increment precedes the read. R03-01 pins that exact boundary, which is why the >= sabotage turns it red.

sabotage.control: the ownership gate stops comparing subject_id to the requested id
a missing cf-connecting-ip shares one 'unknown' bucket
the abuse gate moved after the body parse

not_claimed: R01 verifies refusal on the GET surfaces of the eight named routes. It does not enumerate every method on every one of the 54.
The rate-limit window expiry (10 minutes) is not exercised; these cases all run inside one window.
